title: U.S. Bank Reserves at Fed Edge Lower to $2.93 Trillion, Signaling Slight Liquidity Pullback
body: Reserve balances held by depository institutions at the Federal Reserve declined to $2.928 trillion, down from a previous level of $3.001 trillion, according to data updated on 27 November 2026. The modest decrease in balances suggests a small withdrawal of excess liquidity from the U.S. banking system. While the move is not dramatic in scale, shifts in reserve levels are closely watched by markets for clues about underlying funding conditions and the stance and impact of Federal Reserve policy tools. The latest reading indicates that banks are operating with slightly lower reserves than in the prior period, a development that may influence short-term money market dynamics and inform investor expectations around future Federal Reserve operations and liquidity management. title: Fed Trims Balance Sheet to $6.73 Trillion as Quantitative Tightening Continues
body: The U.S. Federal Reserve has modestly reduced the size of its balance sheet, with total assets edging down to $6,732 billion from $6,741 billion, according to data updated on 27 November 2026. The roughly $9 billion decline underscores the central bank's ongoing commitment to gradually unwind the extraordinary stimulus measures put in place during recent crises. While the week-to-week move is small in absolute terms, it is consistent with the Fed's broader strategy of quantitative tightening, aimed at normalizing monetary conditions after years of aggressive bond purchases. A shrinking balance sheet typically works in tandem with interest rate policy, influencing overall financial conditions and liquidity in the banking system. Investors and analysts will continue to watch the pace and composition of the Fed's balance sheet runoff as a key signal of how aggressively policymakers are willing to restrain credit and temper inflationary pressures, without unduly tightening financial markets or harming growth. title: Ibovespa Pares Gains as Trabuco Euphoria Cools
body: The Ibovespa pared earlier gains to trade near 177,000 points on Friday, after jumping at the opening as initial euphoria over the appointment of Luiz Carlos Trabuco, chairman of Bradesco's board, as Finance Minister faded. Petrobras weighed on the benchmark, dropping more than 3% as oil prices turned lower on worries about a looming supply surplus and continued strong crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Vale also retreated about 3%, pressured by falling iron ore prices amid weakening demand and expectations of higher global supply. The rally in financials lost momentum as well: Bradesco held on to a modest gain after rising more than 6% at its intraday high, Banco do Brasil was up just over 1% after having climbed as much as 8%, and B3 advanced around 6% following an earlier jump of up to 11%. Brazilian equities had been buoyed by speculation over Trabuco's nomination, and the official confirmation, announced after Thursday's close, helped resolve a source of uncertainty that had weighed on local financial assets amid concerns about the country's fiscal outlook. title: Wall Street Gains as AI Trade Rebounds
body: US stocks finished higher in Friday's shortened session, rebounding from pre-Thanksgiving losses as the AI trade regained momentum. The S&P 500 climbed 1.6%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 592 points, and the Nasdaq 100 gained 2.6%, staging a strong rally after nearing bear-market territory earlier in the week. Chipmakers and AI-focused hyperscalers led the move, with Micron surging 7.6%, AMD up 4.6%, Broadcom advancing 3.8% and Meta rising 3.1%. Investors sought to extend the dip-buying that emerged late Wednesday, even as concerns linger over higher borrowing costs and the potential for tighter AI regulation. Nvidia lagged the broader AI rally, adding just 0.8% following reports that its Blackwell chips—barred from sale to China—are being used in a Shanghai data center tied to Nvidia client Megaspeed, formerly overseen by Alice Huang, who is suspected of links to Beijing's intelligence services. For the week, the S&P 500 gained 1.3%, the Dow rose 1,551 points, and the Nasdaq 100 inched up 0.3%. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Wasted Wind and Solar Power Could Run Factories and Data Centers
body: As the scale and reach of variable renewable energies expand around the world, more and more clean energy is being produced. However, more and more of that clean energy is also going to waste. In order to balance energy supply and demand, electric utilities rely on a process called curtailment, where they deliberately reduce the amount of energy produced by solar and wind farms in order to not overwhelm the energy grid. But a new MIT study asks: what if that excess clean energy could be used to power some of the United States' dirtiest sectors?…
